findings.title: Verifier certifies attacker-controlled text without verifying any signature
findings.evidence: Lines 62-103 only call content.contains; line 84 searches a hardware-signature label; lines 108-114 print absolute certification. The file imports only std. scripts/c5_demos/c5_sovereign_compliance_orchestrator.py:99-104 compiles and runs this CLI.
findings.trigger: Pass --pack a plaintext file containing the searched labels, one quoted PASS token, and the two exact final status substrings, with no valid JSON, signature, chain, or proof.
findings.impact: The demo reports a valid hardware signature, intact zero-knowledge proof, and absolute compliance for unauthenticated bytes; it cannot serve as an evidence verifier. No runtime authorization bypass is inferred.

findings.title: Unknown obligations silently become successful empty verification
findings.evidence: verify_statement_content drops unknown obligation strings in the wildcard arm. omega0.rs:142-144 returns true when obligations is empty.
findings.trigger: Call verify_statement_content with valid modality and only an unknown or misspelled obligation such as reproduciblity.
findings.impact: The Python-facing verification API returns true after removing the requested constraint instead of rejecting unsupported obligations.

findings.title: Contradiction verification ignores kernel nogoods
findings.evidence: The method calls omega0::verify(&js), which constructs an empty nogoods set at omega0.rs:133-134; Contradiction merely checks absence from that set at lines 152-154. contradict_knowledge updates self.atms at bindings.rs:112-119 but this verification method never queries it.
findings.trigger: Assert a contradiction for content X, then call verify_statement_content(X, epistemic, [contradiction]).
findings.impact: The API returns true for an obligation that the same kernel state marks contradicted. This is a verification-result defect, not a proven execution-gate bypass.

findings.title: Property tests do not exercise the engine whose concurrency they claim to check
findings.evidence: Lines 263-267 clamp generated integers with min(c, limit), then assert the clamp is <= limit. The file imports no production BFT/KDA implementation; other tests similarly construct local dictionaries and duplicate formulas.
findings.trigger: Change or break the production BFT concurrency limiter and run this property suite.
findings.impact: The concurrency test remains satisfied regardless of the production limiter, so it cannot detect the stated regression; use generated DAGs against the actual engine.

findings.title: Relative transformation breaks the root-position invariant for subsequent transforms
findings.evidence: r_transform([60,64,67], True) returns [60,64,69], False; p_transform assumes the second element is the minor third and increments it. Composition therefore yields [60,65,69] instead of an A-major pitch set [61,64,69]. generate_tonnetz_walk repeatedly feeds these arrays into transforms at lines 83-88.
findings.trigger: Select the P-R alternating mode or any walk with a major R followed by minor P.
findings.impact: The generated progression leaves the intended Neo-Riemannian transformations because inverted relative triads are interpreted as root-position triads.

findings.title: Architecture manifest points its formal foundation to a missing proof path
findings.evidence: The foundation and section 2 link docs/proof/lean/BabylonTrace.lean; a targeted read reports No such file or directory. The whitepaper instead links proof/lean/BabylonTrace.lean.
findings.trigger: Follow the formal-foundation or bisimulation link from this manifest.
findings.impact: Readers cannot inspect the cited proof through the documented reference.
